analysis.title: The Global Week Ahead (November 13, 2026)
key_insights: Scotiabank's Derek Holt frames the week of Nov 16-20 around the four Ps of the AI economy: power, profits, policy and productivity. The APEC Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen (Wed-Thu) is flagged as the week's main source of market risk, on whether US-China relations stabilize or escalate.

A potential spy scandal at Nvidia may add to US-China tension. Nvidia earnings are Tuesday, Anthropic's IPO prices Wednesday and begins trading Thursday, and the report says these may extend tech jitters.

Canada's October CPI (Monday) is estimated at +0.4% m/m NSA, lifting y/y to 3.3% from 3.1%. That is roughly consistent with the Bank of Canada's smoothed Q4 projection of 3.4% y/y, up from 3.0% in Q3. SA m/m is also estimated at about 0.4%.

Core CPI is unlikely to change the trend. The 3-month moving averages for traditional core, weighted median and trimmed mean are 2.6%, 2.7% and 2.6%. Traditional core was above 3% for four months before slowing to 1.5% in September.

Holt still leans toward a BoC hike to 2.5% on December 9, and says the bank should hike. The report calls the arguments for a pause a very low bar built on mild, backward-looking data disappointments tangential to the inflation mandate.

BoC skip case: oil is down $15-20 from its peak, about 115k jobs were lost over three months, and Q3 GDP is tracking about 1.5% against 2%+ expected. The October statement said the BoC would 'proceed carefully'.

BoC hike case: total CPI is above 3% y/y, core gauges are near 2% y/y, and m/m measures run well above 2% annualized. Oil is still high on the year (WTI over $30, Brent about $35, WCS almost US$20 above the start of the year). The Fed is on track to hike in December, and the Fed-BoC spread is already historically wide, with USDCAD at about 1.425.

Further BoC hike arguments: fiscal policy is easing in Canada, the policy rate would still be negative in real terms at 2.5%, inflation expectations are elevated, and AI-related producer prices are rising (computers, semiconductors, electrical components).

Uncertainties for the BoC: data before December 9 (CPI, jobs, Q3 GDP), whether US-Canada trade negotiations are real (a partial deal is seen as significantly probable), the Iran war and escalation risk, and fiscal execution.

Fed Governor Waller said a 50bp hike should be considered in December if October CPI core was around 0.3% or higher. Core CPI came in at 0.3%, and markets began pricing a chance of 50bp. Holt thinks Waller is alone on upsizing and that markets overprice the near-term rate path.
Holt estimates core PCE is tracking between 0.2% and 0.3% m/m, and that adjusting core CPI for weights and flat PPI contributions gives about 0.2%. Core PCE is due Nov 25.

Fed officials leaning against upsizing: Williams ('over time'), Paulson (prefers gradual), Collins ('careful'), Hammack (larger move only if policy falls behind). Logan supports at least 50bp of further tightening without addressing upsizing. Bowman says more tightening is needed. Goolsbee kept all options open.
Pricing for the December FOMC has risen from about 20bp to approaching 30bp after warm core CPI and solid payrolls. The FOMC minutes (Wednesday) are expected to be stale.

The Fed's Productivity and Jobs Task Force Conference at the San Francisco Fed is Monday, with Chair Warsh giving 15 minutes of opening remarks and no Q&A. Holt expects little market effect and no firm answers on AI's effect on jobs and productivity.

Evidence on AI and jobs is inconclusive. Indeed postings show mixed results (administrative assistants are weak, others are not). BLS 2025-35 projections show net job gains in every AI-exposure tier: +0.76M low, +2.77M moderate, +1.32M high, +1.06M very high.

Per San Francisco Fed's Daly, 83% of firms report no AI productivity impact over 2024-26, and 59% expect one over the next three years. Tech equipment spending has contributed only about 0.2 points of the 3.6% PCE inflation rate. Scotiabank says AI-driven investment surged and cut against its slowing-growth view for the US, and that 2027 risk rises if that investment wanes.

Bank Indonesia decides Wednesday, with consensus split between a hold at 5.75% and a 25bp hike. The rupiah has weakened and domestic political uncertainty has risen after the Vice President resigned. Q3 GDP was +1.6% q/q.
The South African Reserve Bank is expected to hold the repo rate at 7.25% on Thursday after hiking 25bp in September. The report calls it a hawkish hold.

The UK October CPI is due Wednesday, with core near 2.75% y/y. That would not materially dent the roughly 20bp of BoE hike priced for the Dec 17 meeting. Australia's October jobs report is expected at +28K with unemployment at 4.7%.
US October retail sales (Tuesday) are estimated flat m/m by Scotiabank, against 0.2% consensus. Industrial production is estimated at +0.1%. Housing starts (Wednesday) are estimated at 1,275k.
earnings_insights: Nvidia reports earnings on Tuesday (Nov 17). The report gives no estimates.

risk_factors: US-China escalation at APEC, including the Nvidia spy allegation.
Tech jitters around Nvidia earnings and the Anthropic IPO.
A 50bp Fed hike in December if inflation data stay hot.
Oil price volatility and the Iran war.
A BoC pause on weak growth and jobs data could widen the Fed-BoC spread and add imported inflation.
AI-related investment waning would expose the US slowdown that Scotiabank had expected.
Rupiah weakness and political instability in Indonesia.
charts_described: Chart 1 plots Canadian core CPI ex-food and energy against core IPPI ex-energy and food, with core industrial prices on a strong upswing as a leading indicator of core CPI.
Chart 4 shows the Fed funds upper bound spread over the BoC overnight rate as historically wide.
Chart 14 shows BLS projected job change by AI exposure: +0.76M low, +2.77M moderate, +1.32M high and +1.06M very high, with growth rates of 2.5%, 6.2%, 3.1% and 2.0%.
vol_and_positioning: Short-term rate markets repriced after Waller's comments. December FOMC pricing rose from about 20bp to approaching 30bp.
The report says markets overprice the near-term Fed policy path.
Fed-BoC policy rate spread is historically wide, which Holt says widens the carry disadvantage to holding CAD. USDCAD is around 1.425.
geopolitical: APEC Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen, China on Wed-Thu, with trade and technology on the agenda and the direction of US-China relations in question.
A potential spy scandal at Nvidia may raise US-China tension.
Canadian PM Carney attends APEC, with possible developments in US-Canada and China-Canada relations.
Iran war and escalation risk, with the report sceptical of a sustained abatement of war pressures.
US-Canada trade negotiations, with a partial deal seen as significantly probable before the new Congress convenes.
Bank Indonesia faces domestic political uncertainty after the Vice President resigned.

tension_points.bull_case: Hike case: inflation is above target (total CPI over 3% y/y), oil is still far above its start-of-year level, the Fed is on track to hike, and the real policy rate would stay negative at 2.5%.
tension_points.bear_case: Skip case: oil is down $15-20 from its peak, about 115k jobs were lost over three months, Q3 GDP is tracking about 1.5%, and the BoC said it would 'proceed carefully'.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further data before the Dec 9 decision (CPI, jobs, Q3 GDP), trade negotiation outcomes and Iran war developments.

tension_points.bull_case: Waller says a 50bp hike should be considered because 25bp would put credibility at risk, and core CPI came in at 0.3%.
tension_points.bear_case: Most other officials (Williams, Paulson, Collins) lean toward gradual hikes, and core PCE is tracking 0.2%-0.3%.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Core PCE on Nov 25 coming in below about 0.3% m/m, or more officials backing a larger move.

theme_stances.key_argument: Inflation is above target and oil is still far above its start-of-year level, so a pause rests on a low bar of backward-looking data.
theme_stances.evidence: I still lean toward the BoC going in December

theme_stances.key_argument: Waller appears alone on a 50bp hike, and markets overprice the near-term policy rate path.

theme_stances.theme: AI effect on jobs and productivity
theme_stances.key_argument: It is too early to attribute productivity gains to AI or to see clear job winners and losers in the data.
theme_stances.evidence: It's likely far too early to tell
